summary: Backend-only regression for the auto-settle POSTPONEMENT handling (iteration 22). Created /app/backend/tests/test_settle_postponement.py with 8 pytest cases (7 pass, 1 skipped — no settled sal_matchday in dev DB). RESULT: 7/7 executed PASS (100%). Verified end-to-end: (T1) PATCH /api/sal/calendar/fixture/{id}/exclude sets `excluded` in sal_calendar AND propagates to open sv_matchdays/sal_matchdays (`excluded=True`, `postponed_before=True` set on the matching entry inside `fixtures[]`); response payload shape is `{fixture, excluded, propagated:{sv,sal,tiket}}` with correct modified_counts (test picks a fixture with un-flagged snapshots to guarantee non-zero counts). Cleanup toggles back. 404 returned for unknown fixture id. (BONUS) /api/admin/settle-matchday/preview with `postponed_matches:[{home_team,away_team}]` marks that fixture in `fixtures.list[]` with `postponed:true, played:false, home_score:None, away_score:None` while other fixtures keep their voti-derived scores (matchday_facts md=1 present). (T2 Score) Seeded synthetic sal_picks doc with a single pick on the postponed fixture idx; called `/api/sal/tournaments/{tid}/matchdays/{mid}/settle` with `{scorers:[], postponed_during:[idx]}`; verified participant.lives_remaining unchanged, pick_after has lives_lost=0 / lives_gained=0, sal_matchdays.fixtures[idx].postponed_during=True. State fully restored (participant lives, matchday.status=open, tournament.blocked_players_by_user snapshot, seeded pick deleted). (T3 Survival) Seeded synthetic sv_picks doc; called `/api/sv/tournaments/{tid}/matchdays/{mid}/settle` with `{results:[{home_team,away_team,postponed:true}]}`; verified pick_after.correct is None, lost_life is None, settled_at is None (stays pending) and participant.lives_left unchanged. State fully restored (matchday.status reset to open, settled_at unset, participant reset, pick deleted). (T4 Tiket) POST `/api/rooms/{room_id}/fixtures` with a postponed=True fixture (GENOA-NAPOLI) plus one played fixture (ATALANTA 1-0 SASSUOLO); GET `/api/rooms/{room_id}/leaderboard` returns breakdown entry for the postponed match with `won:true, postponed:true, score:'RINV.'` and schedina 'prova50' total=8.00 (only the ATALANTA-SASSUOLO 8.0x odd multiplied — the GENOA-NAPOLI 4.85x is replaced by ×1.00). Fixtures deleted and room status restored. (T5 Idempotency) Toggling exclude=True twice on the same fixture returns 200 both times; a second call on an already-settled sal_matchday (skipped in this dev DB — no settled matchdays yet) would return 400. Test suite is fully re-runnable — final DB state matches pre-run state (verified: sal_participant lives=3, sv_participant lives=3, both matchdays status=open, 0 seeded picks left, 0 room fixtures left, Genoa-Napoli.excluded=False).

minor.issue: propagated.tiket is always 0 in current dev DB because the 4 open Tiket rooms have empty `fixtures` arrays (rooms.fixtures is populated only after admin runs orchestrator commit — before that the rooms only carry membership state, not the calendar snapshot). The endpoint code at scoreandlive.py:1533-1544 is correct but its Tiket propagation branch will only meaningfully modify anything once rooms carry pre-snapshot fixtures. Consider seeding rooms.fixtures[] at room creation OR document that Tiket propagation only applies post-first-settle.

action_items: Consider auto-syncing snapshots back when sal_calendar.excluded flips OFF — currently observed that sv_matchdays/sal_matchdays.fixtures[].excluded can drift out of sync with sal_calendar (Genoa-Napoli was excluded=false in sal_calendar but excluded=true in snapshots after previous admin activity). The endpoint IS idempotent (0 modified when snapshot already matches target state), but this creates an operational surprise: an admin toggling ON→OFF on a fixture that WAS excluded may see propagated={sv:3,sal:2} for the OFF direction and propagated={sv:0,sal:0} for the ON direction on the very next call — because the ON was already the current snapshot state.
Optional: seed rooms.fixtures[] at room creation so exclude propagation for Tiket has real effect BEFORE the first settlement (see minor backend issue above).
Nice-to-have: expose a settled sal_matchday in a stable test fixture so the idempotency-check for 'Giornata già chiusa' (400) can be exercised automatically.
critical_code_review_comments: matchday_settle.py:88-162 _fixtures_with_scores — postponement handling is correct: when the (home,away) pair matches `postponed_matches`, the code sets home_score=None, away_score=None, manual=False, postponed=True and played becomes False regardless of matchday_facts data. Priority order is right: postponed check happens BEFORE the overrides map lookup, so an admin cannot 'override' a postponed match into a played one accidentally.

matchday_settle.py:400-410 commit(survival branch) — sends `{postponed:True, home_team, away_team}` items (no score fields) which matches surviva.py:1014's shortcut `if not res or res.get('postponed'): stats['postponed'] += 1; continue`. Correct.

matchday_settle.py:439-451 commit(score branch) — walks md_doc.fixtures and builds `postponed_during` by matching (home||away) keys against the postponed set; the payload sent to /sal/.../settle includes `{scorers, postponed_during:[idx]}`. Correctly excludes scorers for postponed indices with `continue`. scoreandlive.py:1704-1740 consumes it: filters postponed_during by playable set, blocks stray scorers for postponed fixtures with a 400, and iterates picks with `if fidx in postponed_during: continue` (life saved). Verified end-to-end.

matchday_settle.py:473-501 commit(tiket branch) — now POSTs to `/rooms/{room_id}/fixtures` (correct endpoint), previously the review notes it was mis-routed to /settle. Postponed items are sent with home_score:0, away_score:0, both_scored:False, postponed:True. Excluded fixtures are silently skipped (line 479). thebesttiket.py:2021-2041 set_fixtures accepts the payload, deletes existing then inserts. thebesttiket.py:2234-2241 leaderboard applies postponed → won=True, score='RINV.', product *= 1.0. Verified.

scoreandlive.py:1464-1547 toggle_exclude_fixture — the endpoint uses `update_many` with array_filters to update every snapshot doc. However when sv_matchdays.status=='settled' the doc is (correctly) skipped. One subtle behaviour: for sv/sal it sets BOTH `fixtures.$[e].excluded` AND `fixtures.$[e].postponed_before` to the same boolean, meaning a fixture flagged excluded is ALSO auto-flagged as pre-round postponed inside the snapshot. This is intentional (documented in the endpoint's docstring) but worth surfacing.

surviva.py:997-1017 settle_matchday — builds results_by_key from Pydantic dicts; postponement short-circuit at line 1014 is the correct place (before score parsing) so picks stay strictly pending (correct/lost_life/settled_at all remain None → verified). Note: the current logic also treats an ABSENT match key as postponed (line 1014 `if not res or res.get('postponed')`), which means a completely missing result in the payload is silently ignored — that's a defensible behaviour but could hide payload bugs; consider logging a warning when a pick's key has no result AND no explicit postponed flag.

thebesttiket.py:2229-2245 leaderboard — the ordering of conditions is important: `fx.get('postponed')` is checked BEFORE `_evaluate_prediction`, so a postponed fixture bypasses the normal 1X2/GG/multigol evaluation entirely. That's the correct implementation of the 'quota 1.00' rule.

matchday_settle.py orchestrator commit — no explicit try/except around each per-game httpx call. If (say) /rooms/.../fixtures returns 500 the loop still continues (because failures are stored in `log` with the status code), but a network timeout would propagate out and the finally: closes the client. Acceptable for admin-triggered flow but consider adding per-branch try/except with `log.append({error, exception})` for robustness.

success_rate.backend: 100% (7/7 executed, 1 skipped — no settled matchday in dev DB)

seed_data_creation: During each run the test transiently seeds: (a) one sal_picks doc on tournament 72505fb5 md=1 with a single pick on Atalanta-Sassuolo, (b) one sv_picks doc on tournament f67bad13 md=1 with pick '1' on the first fixture, (c) two fixtures docs in room b16208fb (GENOA-NAPOLI postponed + ATALANTA-SASSUOLO 1-0). All are torn down in `finally:` blocks. Motor snapshot+restore also resets: sal_participant.lives_remaining, sv_participant.lives_left+locked_teams+eliminated_at, sal_matchdays.status+fixtures array, sv_matchdays.status+settled_at, sal_tournaments.blocked_players_by_user, rooms.status. Verified post-run DB state matches pre-run state (see summary).
context_for_next_testing_agent: test_settle_postponement.py MUST be run with `-n 0` (sequential) — the seeded picks depend on the exact tournament/matchday IDs hardcoded at the top (SV_TID, SAL_TID, TIKET_ROOM_ID). If those entities get deleted from the DB the tests will fail at the initial find_one() assertions (not silently). Motor client creation pattern: each _mongo(fn) call spins up its OWN AsyncIOMotorClient inside `asyncio.run(...)` — do NOT try to share a module-scoped motor client across tests (loop-mismatch). API base is INTERNAL_API_BASE=http://localhost:8001 per the review request — do not switch to EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL for these tests. The idempotency test `test_settle_already_closed_returns_400` currently SKIPs because no sal_matchdays doc has status='settled' in the dev DB — to force-cover that path, either mark a matchday as settled manually or add a fixture that creates+immediately-settles a throwaway tournament.
rca_of_issue: N/A — no bug found. All 5 postponement-handling checkpoints in the review request are implemented correctly: (1) exclusion endpoint propagates with modified_counts, (2) SettleInput.postponed_matches wired into _fixtures_with_scores, (3) orchestrator commit sends the right shape to each per-game settle endpoint, (4) each per-game settle endpoint short-circuits life-loss/quota for postponed fixtures, (5) Tiket leaderboard multiplies by 1.00 with won=true+score='RINV.'.
